evaluations.label: A
errors: Refers to the project as 'TS3012a', which is never said in the transcript.
Gives inconsistent, garbled names for the same people: 'Markoff', 'Dirk Mangfelt', 'Savier Jokins' (Mark, Dirk Meinfeld, Xavier Juergens).
Says 'Speaker 4 clarifies that the scope is limited to a TV remote control'; the UI designer asked and the Project Manager answered.
Says the industrial designer suggested lightweight materials that are 'aesthetically impactful'; he only said the material should be light.
Action items ('Research current market trends and user needs', 'Design a distinctive, trendy, intuitive TV remote control interface') are generic and unassigned. The meeting assigned neither.
Never gives the UI designer's name (Nick Broer) and leaves him as 'Speaker 4'.
strengths: Most detailed and well-organized account of the meeting: roles, three phases, tools, animal exercise, scope, accessibility, light material.
Correct price figures (25 euros selling, about 12.50 euros production).
Correctly says personal assignments come later and the team reconvenes in 30 minutes.
Lists open questions (multi-remote vs TV only, accessibility, materials).
weaknesses: Action items are generic and not tied to owners or to anything actually assigned.
Leaves out the whiteboard responsiveness complaint.
Redundant: the same material appears in the summary and again in the outline.
Name inconsistencies and an invented project code reduce trust.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Many timestamps are slightly off (for example the three-phase and project-folder points are tagged [01:08], when they are around 01:47 and 03:23).
'Dirk Mengveld' is a garbled spelling of Dirk Meinfeld.
The UI designer is not named (Nick Broer) and appears only as 'the interface designer'.
strengths: Best fidelity to what was said and who said it: Project Manager confirming the TV-only brief, the UI designer's accessibility question, the industrial designer's light-material point, the elephant 'big and strong player in the market' suggestion.
Captures the whiteboard's low responsiveness and preference for pen and paper.
Correctly says the personal coach will give out the individual assignments and the team meets again in 30 minutes.
Notes that the UI designer found 25 euros selling against 12.50 euros production 'not much to work with'.
Gives one realistic action item: the marketing expert shares his ideas at the follow-up, owner identified.
Clear sections and timestamps make it easy to scan.
weaknesses: Only one action item; it omits the Project Manager posting minutes and the individual work for each role.
Omits the industrial designer's three questions.
Slightly wordy, with some repetition between the summary and the sections.

evaluations.label: C
errors: Assigns the Project Manager to 'Provide personal assignments to team members'; he said the personal coach would do that.
Assigns Xavier 'Address material considerations for lightweight design'; no such task was given.
Assigns the UI designer 'Prepare intuitive design concepts'; no such task was given.
Assigns the marketing expert 'Bring marketing insights on user preferences'; this is a loose inference, not a stated commitment.
Describes the dolphin as 'freedom, smooth design'; 'smooth' was never said about it.
Garbled and inconsistent names: 'Mark Knopp', 'Xavier Juukens', 'Dirk Mankveld'.
Timestamps do not match the transcript (for example the scope clarification tagged 10:34 and the pricing tagged 12:10).
Calls the gap before the next meeting a '30-minute break'; it was time for individual work.
strengths: Includes the price figures and the TV-only scope.
Mentions the whiteboard responsiveness issue and the four animal metaphors.
Has an action-item section with named owners.
weaknesses: Most action items are invented or wrongly attributed, which is a serious problem for a section meant to say who does what.
Thin on detail about the discussion (accessibility is mentioned only in passing).
Does not say the personal coach, not the Project Manager, will hand out assignments.

evaluations.label: D
errors: Adds 'openness' to the dolphin and 'precision' to the tiger; neither was said.
Spelling variants: 'Mark Knopf', 'Dirk Mengveld', 'Xavier Jökens'.
Says the UI designer's name was 'not captured'; it is stated in the transcript (Nick Broer).
Does not say who drew which animal, so the exercise is not tied to the people.
strengths: Mostly faithful and does not invent tasks or owners.
Includes the industrial designer's three questions (inside, material, look) and the three-phase plan.
Gets the price figures, the scope confirmation, light material, accessibility and the 30-minute reconvene right.
Correctly notes that the personal coach distributes individual assignments.
weaknesses: No action-items section; the marketing expert's pending ideas and the Project Manager posting minutes are not called out as to-dos.
Does not give the UI designer's contributions (the multi-remote question, the familiarity point, the whiteboard issue) to anyone by name.
Little on the discussion detail, so less useful for someone who missed the meeting.

rationale: B is the most faithful and the most useful. It attributes statements correctly, captures the whiteboard issue, the TV-only scope, accessibility, light material, the 25 euro / 12.50 euro figures, the personal coach and the 30-minute reconvene, and lists one realistic action item with the right owner. A is the most thorough but has an invented project code, a misattributed scope clarification, embellishments, and generic unassigned action items. D is accurate and concise but gives no action items and less detail, and adds small embellishments to the animal traits. C is last because its action items assign tasks that were never given and misattribute the assignment hand-out to the Project Manager (it was the personal coach), which makes its decisions and actions section unreliable.
